corrections.old: Amounts the citizen pays are published line by line for the domestic category: application fee Rs. 10, opening fee Rs. 250 water and Rs. 250 sewer, trade advance Rs. 5,000, occupier security Rs. 500 and Rs. 500, and road restoration Rs. 1,600 and Rs. 3,200 within 5 metres, with fixed development charges of Rs. 45,000 or Rs. 1,00,000 in regularised colonies and a Rs. 50 doorstep fee. The published total is not exhaustive: beyond 5 metres the applicant bears the contractor's cost, which the same route says is not billed by the Board.
corrections.new: The FAQ publishes a line-by-line schedule of amounts the citizen pays in the domestic category, which is this scenario's category: application fee Rs. 10, opening fee Rs. 250 water and Rs. 250 sewer, trade advance Rs. 5,000, occupier security Rs. 500 water and Rs. 500 sewer, and road restoration Rs. 1,600 water and Rs. 3,200 sewer where the distance from the property to the DJB network is up to 5 metres. Two further amounts are route-specific rather than general: the fixed development charge of Rs. 45,000 or Rs. 1,00,000 applies only in unauthorised regularised colonies, which a scoped applicant may or may not live in, and the Rs. 50 doorstep fee only on the optional doorstep route. The FAQ also gives Rs. 10 for the application form and processing; the reviewed evidence does not establish whether that is the same Rs. 10 as the table's application fee, and this ledger does not resolve it. The schedule is not established as exhaustive: no claim in this ledger records what is payable where the distance to the network exceeds 5 metres, and that gap is recorded here as a limitation on the reviewed evidence, not as a finding about what the route says.
corrections.reason: Sections 9 and 13. The closing sentence asserted that beyond 5 metres the applicant bears the contractor's cost and that the same route says the Board does not bill it. No claim in this ledger records any of that, so the sidecar was carrying an uncited evidential assertion in prose. The rewrite keeps the honest point — the schedule is not exhaustive — as a stated limitation, and scopes the route-specific amounts so the note does not read as though they stack for every applicant.

corrections.old: An actionable service-level target is published: 15 days for a new water and sewer connection, named against the responsible officer in the charter's service table, and the same 15 days for the doorstep route. A second figure binds the applicant, who must pay the ZRO's demand within fifteen days or lose the sanction. The 15-day figure covers sanction; no figure is published for the physical installation that follows, which the same evidence says is executed by a licensed plumber at the applicant's cost.
corrections.new: An actionable service-level target is published: the charter's table of services gives 15 days for a new water and sewer connection, and the charter gives the same 15 days for the doorstep route, where its wording ties the figure to sanction of the connection. The figure therefore covers one stage only. The reviewed evidence publishes no figure for anything that follows sanction, and this ledger records that a demand raised by the ZRO office must then be paid within fifteen days or the sanction is withdrawn — a deadline binding on the applicant, not a service-level target on the Board. What is required after that payment, and how long it takes, is not established by the reviewed evidence and is recorded here as a limitation. Both charter figures rest on a source whose currency is not established by the document and which audit grades C; the only Grade B figure in this cell is the applicant's own payment deadline.
corrections.reason: Sections 8, 9 and 13. Section 8 requires the note to say when a time figure covers only one stage, which the original did; but the same sentence asserted that the stage which follows is a physical installation executed by a licensed plumber at the applicant's cost, and no claim in this ledger records any of that. The original also stated the 15 days is named against the responsible officer in the charter's service table, which no claim establishes. The rewrite keeps the one-stage disclosure section 8 demands, states the post-sanction gap as a limitation, and records the grade position after the F1 downgrades.

support.auditNote: Audit finding F6, with F1. Cell state unchanged at stated: a published 15-day delivery time in a charter's table of services is a service-level target under section 8, and the one-stage condition attached to that definition is satisfied by this note. Claim IDs are unchanged.
